claim: Control LNP61 delivered mRNA to N% of liver endothelial cells
locus_A: Fig. 3C pentagon numeral: Li (54,81) -- the second value, green, pairs with the dotted Control trace
locus_B: Results text: "whereas Control LNP61 delivered mRNA to 66% of splenic macrophages and 82% of liver endothelial cells"
measurement: 81 vs 82, a 1 percentage-point difference; on this experiment's z-scale (log10 sd 0.104806) the two candidates differ by 0.051 z

claim: GlycoLNP61 and Control LNP61 percent Thy1.1+ splenic macrophages at 0.8 mg/kg
locus_B: Fig. 3D dose-response bars, 0.8 mpk: digitised 88.03 (Glyco) and 46.37 (Control); ticks 384.032/480.0/576.077 px, LOO residual 0.109 px against a 1.5 px strict tolerance, 0.5207 percent per px
measurement: Glyco x1.129 HIGHER in Fig. 3D; Control x0.703 LOWER. The paper's own effect size Glyco/Control is 1.1818 from Fig. 3C and 1.8984 from Fig. 3D -- a ratio of ratios of 1.6064, with the two panels disagreeing in OPPOSITE directions
why: Same formulation, same 0.8 mg/kg dose, same organ, same cell type, same 16 h timepoint, different cohorts (Fig. 3A shows ~12 points per bar, Fig. 3D shows 3). The digitisation is not in doubt: Fig. 3D's own dose response is strictly decreasing (88.03 > 77.10 > 26.59) and every bar passed bars.bar_top with flank delta 0.0. This is a property of the paper. Printed numerals outrank a bar read, so Fig. 3C is emitted, and Fig. 3D is recorded here rather than averaged in. See DECISIONS D-4.

claim: Fig. S4 shows the ranking of GlycoLNPs by spleen-to-liver ratio
locus_A: SI caption: "Fig. S4. Schematic showing the process of ranking GlycoLNPs based on their spleen-to-liver ratios and selecting the winner LNPs."
locus_B: The panel itself, read at native 219.8 dpi: five stylised barcode combs, a four-bar chart whose categories are labelled A/B/C/D, and prose describing a two-list rule
measurement: Zero LNP names and zero numbers appear in the panel. The bar chart's y axis is "Thy1.1+ Cells (%)" with ticks at 0/5/10/15/20 but its x categories are the letters A-D, not cell types or LNPs
why: The caption describes a ranking the figure does not contain. The ranked list the Results text refers to ("We ranked GlycoLNPs based on their spleen-to-liver ratios (SI Appendix, Fig. S4) and selected five lead GlycoLNPs") is not published anywhere in the article or SI. This is the single largest gap between what the study measured and what it reports.

claim: Fig. 2A and Fig. S5 give different PDIs for the same five LNPs
measurement: Rounding Fig. 2A to ONE SIGNIFICANT FIGURE reproduces Fig. S5 on 5 of 5. A one-DECIMAL-place rule scores only 3/5, failing on exactly the two values below 0.1
what_we_emitted: the Fig. 2A values, which carry the extra digit
why: RETRACTED. There is no contradiction: Fig. S5 prints Fig. 2A's PDIs at one significant figure. It was the rule I first tested that was wrong, not the transcription, and the two failures it produced were precisely the two sub-0.1 values a significant-figure rule treats differently. Dh and EE are byte-identical between the two figures.

claim: The abstract's "109 chemically distinct LNPs" implies 109 distinct lipids
locus_A: Abstract: "Using DNA barcoding to test 109 chemically distinct LNPs in vivo"
locus_B: Results: two libraries of 64, built from 2 ionizable lipids x 4 PEG-lipids x 2 glycolipids x 8 molar-ratio sets; 52 and 57 passed the biophysical screen
measurement: 4 x 2 x 8 = 64 exactly, 2 x 64 = 128 designed, 52 + 57 = 109 injected, 19 discarded
why: RETRACTED as a contradiction. 109 is the number of distinct FORMULATIONS and the Results text says so plainly. Recorded because the phrase is easy to misread as 109 distinct chemical entities when the screen contains exactly TWO ionizable lipids, both of them already in this corpus, and the varying component is the helper lipid.
